title: Disclose trade-offs in US emissions rule change | Science
description: In September, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rolled back Biden-era greenhouse gas emissions standards for fossil fuel–fired electric generating units without quantifying the likely adverse health effects (1). A year earlier, the EPA had estimated that such a change would lead to hundreds of additional deaths annually (1, 2). The agency’s decision to exclude the evidence of harm from its deregulation of greenhouse gas emissions reverses a long-standing federal practice to provide policy-makers and the public with quantitative estimates of benefits and costs of major regulatory decisions. To ensure public accountability, US agencies should continue this long-standing tradition of promoting transparency.
